yaml.title: SOLID Refactor + 51% Rule Removal + H3 Resolution 11
yaml.author: robin

sectionContent.1. Algorithm Simplification — Removed 51:
The hex capture algorithm was over-engineered. The "51% boundary intersection ratio" check was removed entirely. The new algorithm uses exactly 2 rules:

1. **Trail cells**: Any H3 cell whose center the path crosses through → claimed
2. **Interior fill**: If path forms a closed loop, any H3 cell whose center is inside the loop polygon → claimed

No boundary overlap math. No percentage thresholds. Simple point-in-polygon test.
sectionContent.2. Full Backend SOLID Refactor:
Every backend service rewritten to follow SOLID principles:

**Architecture changes:**
- All services now have proper interfaces (`IHexGridService`, `ITerritoryService`, `IUserService`, `ILeaderboardService`, `IGeoService`, `IValidationService`)
- All dependencies injected via constructor (no `new` keywords)
- No method exceeds 40 lines
- `ClaimResult` uses static factory pattern: `ClaimResult.Failure(error)`, `ClaimResult.Succeeded(data)`
- Separate `GeoService` for geographic calculations (Haversine distance, polygon area)
- Separate `ValidationService` for input validation
- `ClaimsController` extracted from `TerritoryController` (was getting fat)
- All model files split: one class per file

**HexGridService decomposition:**
- `ComputeCapturedCells` — orchestrator (trail + fill)
- `AddTrailCells` — GPS points → H3 cell IDs
- `AddLoopFillCells` — detect loops, fill interiors
- `ExtractLoops` / `FindClosureLoops` — loop detection (path self-intersection)
- `BuildRepairedPolygon` — NTS polygon from loop points
- `DeduplicatePolygons` / `IsDuplicateOf` — overlap detection
- `FillPolygonInteriors` — H3 polyfill via NTS

**TerritoryService decomposition:**
- `ProcessClaim` orchestrator → `ValidateClaim`, `CreateClaimEntity`, `AssignCells`
- Cell assignment → `IsOnCooldown`, `CreateTransfer`, `UpdateExistingCell`, `CreateNewCell`
- Stats → `UpdateUserStats`, `UpdateStreak`, `DecrementVictimHexCounts`
sectionContent.3. Frontend Journey Feature Refactor:
**New classes extracted:**
- `LoopDetector` — static class mirroring backend `ExtractLoops` algorithm (counts loops client-side)
- `HexTerritoryManager` — manages hex loading/state (`loadUserOwnHexes`, `loadWideArea`, `loadViewport`, `updateFromCells`, `addCapturedHexes`)
- `CelebrationDialog` — standalone widget (was inline in journey_screen)

**JourneyScreen decomposition:**
- Extracted widgets: `_CircleButton`, `_HexOwnerSheet`, `_StatsBar`, `_BottomControls`
- Map build split: `_buildMap`, `_buildTileLayer`, `_buildOtherPlayerHexes`, etc.
sectionContent.4. H3 Resolution Change (10 → 11): Bumped from resolution 10 (~65m cells) to resolution 11 (~29m edge, ~2,150m² area). Cells feel more "earnable" per walk — a short walk captures meaningful territory. Resolution 10 cells were too large for satisfying single-walk claims.
sectionContent.5. Constants Consolidation:
All magic numbers eliminated. `GameConstants` now contains:
- `MinLoopPoints = 20` — minimum path points before loop detection kicks in
- `LoopSkipNeighbors = 10` — skip nearby points when searching for loop closure

## What Was Built

### 1. Algorithm Simplification — Removed 51% Boundary Rule

The hex capture algorithm was over-engineered. The "51% boundary intersection ratio" check was removed entirely. The new algorithm uses exactly 2 rules:

1. **Trail cells**: Any H3 cell whose center the path crosses through → claimed
2. **Interior fill**: If path forms a closed loop, any H3 cell whose center is inside the loop polygon → claimed

No boundary overlap math. No percentage thresholds. Simple point-in-polygon test.

### 2. Full Backend SOLID Refactor

Every backend service rewritten to follow SOLID principles:

**Architecture changes:**
- All services now have proper interfaces (`IHexGridService`, `ITerritoryService`, `IUserService`, `ILeaderboardService`, `IGeoService`, `IValidationService`)
- All dependencies injected via constructor (no `new` keywords)
- No method exceeds 40 lines
- `ClaimResult` uses static factory pattern: `ClaimResult.Failure(error)`, `ClaimResult.Succeeded(data)`
- Separate `GeoService` for geographic calculations (Haversine distance, polygon area)
- Separate `ValidationService` for input validation
- `ClaimsController` extracted from `TerritoryController` (was getting fat)
- All model files split: one class per file

**HexGridService decomposition:**
- `ComputeCapturedCells` — orchestrator (trail + fill)
- `AddTrailCells` — GPS points → H3 cell IDs
- `AddLoopFillCells` — detect loops, fill interiors
- `ExtractLoops` / `FindClosureLoops` — loop detection (path self-intersection)
- `BuildRepairedPolygon` — NTS polygon from loop points
- `DeduplicatePolygons` / `IsDuplicateOf` — overlap detection
- `FillPolygonInteriors` — H3 polyfill via NTS

**TerritoryService decomposition:**
- `ProcessClaim` orchestrator → `ValidateClaim`, `CreateClaimEntity`, `AssignCells`
- Cell assignment → `IsOnCooldown`, `CreateTransfer`, `UpdateExistingCell`, `CreateNewCell`
- Stats → `UpdateUserStats`, `UpdateStreak`, `DecrementVictimHexCounts`

### 3. Frontend Journey Feature Refactor

**New classes extracted:**
- `LoopDetector` — static class mirroring backend `ExtractLoops` algorithm (counts loops client-side)
- `HexTerritoryManager` — manages hex loading/state (`loadUserOwnHexes`, `loadWideArea`, `loadViewport`, `updateFromCells`, `addCapturedHexes`)
- `CelebrationDialog` — standalone widget (was inline in journey_screen)

**JourneyScreen decomposition:**
- Extracted widgets: `_CircleButton`, `_HexOwnerSheet`, `_StatsBar`, `_BottomControls`
- Map build split: `_buildMap`, `_buildTileLayer`, `_buildOtherPlayerHexes`, etc.

### 4. H3 Resolution Change (10 → 11)

Bumped from resolution 10 (~65m cells) to resolution 11 (~29m edge, ~2,150m² area). Cells feel more "earnable" per walk — a short walk captures meaningful territory. Resolution 10 cells were too large for satisfying single-walk claims.

### 5. Constants Consolidation

All magic numbers eliminated. `GameConstants` now contains:
- `MinLoopPoints = 20` — minimum path points before loop detection kicks in
- `LoopSkipNeighbors = 10` — skip nearby points when searching for loop closure
- `DeduplicationOverlapThreshold = 0.80` — two polygons sharing >80% area are considered duplicates
- `MaxPreviewPathLength = 10_000` — path preview endpoint limit
- `MinPointsForPolygon = 4` — minimum points to attempt polygon construction
- `MinFillAreaSquareMeters = 5_000.0` — loops smaller than 5,000m² only get trail cells (was 30,000)
- `CellCooldownHours = 5.0` — cell can't be re-stolen within 5 hours
- Removed: `MinIntersectionRatio` (was 0.51 — the 51% rule)

## Decisions Made

- **Algorithm**: 2-rule system (trail + center-inside-loop). No boundary overlap.
- **Resolution 11**: Smaller cells = more satisfying gameplay loop per walk
- **Min fill area reduced**: 5,000m² (down from 30,000m²) — because smaller cells at res 11 mean loops produce fewer cells; low threshold keeps fill viable for reasonable-sized walks
- **Cell cooldown**: 5 hours before a cell can be stolen again (anti-grief)
- **Static factories on ClaimResult**: cleaner than constructor overloads

- Committed as `d00a036` on `dev/hex-map-features`
- Merged to `master` (commit `8e5d800`) via `--no-ff`
- Both branches pushed to GitHub

H3 resolution bumped to 11. Frontend journey feature decomposed into LoopDetector, HexTerritoryManager, CelebrationDialog."

- Need real-device testing to confirm resolution 11 feels right
- 5,000m² min fill area — does this produce too many filled hexes for small loops?
- Cell cooldown (5h) — is this balanced for competitive play?

- Real-device testing with resolution 11 cells
- Connect achievements to real progress data
- Implement push notifications for stolen cells

# Progression System

## Key Behaviors
Players earn XP from every hex capture, distance walked, and mission completion. XP drives a level system. Daily missions provide 3 adaptive challenges per day. Achievements (30 total, 7 categories) unlock permanently at stat thresholds and award bonus XP.

sectionContent.Components:
**API Services:**
- **MissionService** (`api/MyLoop.Api/Services/MissionService.cs`): Generates 3 adaptive daily missions, records progress, awards XP. Single save point via `AwardXp`. Race-condition safe (DbUpdateException catch → ChangeTracker.Clear() → re-fetch).
- **AchievementService** (`api/MyLoop.Api/Services/AchievementService.cs`): Checks all 30 achievements against user stats, unlocks qualifying ones with convergence loop for cascading level-ups. Does NOT save — caller saves.
- **Achievement Definitions** (`api/MyLoop.Api/Constants/Achievements.cs`): Static catalog of 30 achievements in 7 categories.

**Key Patterns:**
- **Single-save-point**: `RecordProgress` and `CheckAndUnlock` mutate tracked entities but don't call `SaveChangesAsync`. `AwardXp` is the sole save point for the entire step-claim operation.
- **Concurrent unlock safety**: `AwardXp` wraps `SaveChangesAsync` in try/catch for `DbUpdateException` — detaches conflicting achievement inserts and retries.
- **Convergence loop**: `CheckAndUnlock` loops until no new achievements unlock (handles XP from one achievement triggering a Level achievement).
- **Adaptive mission generation**: Player tier (Newcomer/Regular/Veteran/Elite) × behavior weights → weighted selection with type diversity enforcement.
sectionContent.XP System:
| Source | Amount |
|--------|--------|
| Hex capture | 10 XP |
| Hex stolen | 25 XP |
| Per km walked | 50 XP |
| Streak bonus | 20 XP |
| All missions complete | 100 XP bonus |
| Mission completion | Per-mission XP (varies by tier) |
| Achievement unlock | Per-achievement (25–1000 XP) |

**Level Formula**: `XpForLevel(n) = (n-1)² × 100`
- Level 1 = 0 XP, Level 2 = 100, Level 5 = 1,600, Level 10 = 8,100, Level 50 = 240,100
- `LevelFromXp(xp) = 1 + (int)√(xp / 100)`

**Generation Algorithm:**

2. `ComputeBehaviorWeights`: Based on DistanceKm, TotalHexesCaptured, TopThreeFinishes, Streak, HexCount
3. `WeightedSelect` with type diversity enforcement (no duplicates)
4. Deterministic seed: `XOR(userId.bytes[0..3], userId.bytes[4..7]) ^ date.DayNumber`

**Mission Types:**
- `CaptureHexes` (N hexes)
- `WalkDistance` (~30m per hex, approximate)
- `StealHex` (capture from another player)
- `ExploreNewArea` (claim cells never visited before)
- `MaintainStreak` (keep streak alive today)
- `CaptureInOneWalk` (N hexes in single session)

- Flutter `missions_slice` applies delta without API call

- Flutter `xp_slice` applies — home page XP bar updates in real-time

- Race condition on mission generation: Two requests generate same day's missions simultaneously → DbUpdateException caught, ChangeTracker cleared, re-fetch existing missions
- All 30 achievements already unlocked: Loop body skips everything (HashSet check), exits immediately
- User with 0 stats: All thresholds ≥1, no unlocks triggered, all progress = 0.0

## File Map

### Backend
- `api/MyLoop.Api/Services/MissionService.cs` — Mission generation, progress recording, XP awarding (with concurrency retry)
- `api/MyLoop.Api/Services/AchievementService.cs` — Achievement checking with convergence loop
- `api/MyLoop.Api/Constants/Achievements.cs` — 30 static achievement definitions
- `api/MyLoop.Api/Constants/GameConstants.cs` — XP values, level formula, missions per day
- `api/MyLoop.Api/Controllers/MissionsController.cs` — GET /api/missions/{userId}, GET /api/missions/xp/{userId}
- `api/MyLoop.Api/Controllers/AchievementsController.cs` — GET /api/achievements/{userId} [Authorize]
- `api/MyLoop.Api/Entities/DailyMission.cs` — Mission entity (Id, UserId, Date, Type, Target, Progress, XpReward, CompletedAt)
- `api/MyLoop.Api/Entities/UserAchievement.cs` — Achievement unlock record (Id, UserId, AchievementId, UnlockedAt, XpAwarded)
- `api/MyLoop.Api/Entities/User.cs` — Added: TotalXp, Level, TotalHexesStolen, AllMissionsCompleteDays
- `api/MyLoop.Api/Models/TrailClaimResult.cs` — StepClaimResponse includes XpGained, LeveledUp, NewLevel, AchievementsUnlocked

### Frontend
- `mobile/lib/shared/models/daily_mission.dart` — DailyMission + XpInfo models. `copyWith({int? currentProgress, bool? isCompleted, DateTime? completedAt})` + `bool get completed` convenience getter.
- `mobile/lib/shared/models/achievement.dart` — Achievement model with category name getter. `copyWith({bool? unlocked, DateTime? unlockedAt, double? progress})`.
- `mobile/lib/shared/models/trail_claim_response.dart` — StepClaimResponse + AchievementUnlocked
- `mobile/lib/shared/services/api_service.dart` — getDailyMissions, getXpInfo, getAchievements, getGameState
- `mobile/lib/shared/services/territory_realtime_service.dart` — SignalR event streams: MissionDelta, XpDelta, AchievementUnlocked
- `mobile/lib/shared/state/xp_slice.dart` — XpState Notifier, hydrate() + applyDelta(XpDelta)
- `mobile/lib/shared/state/missions_slice.dart` — MissionsState Notifier, hydrate() + applyDelta(MissionDelta)
- `mobile/lib/shared/state/achievements_slice.dart` — AchievementsState Notifier, hydrate() + applyDelta(AchievementDelta)
- `mobile/lib/features/home/home_tab.dart` — _DailyMissionsCard + _AchievementsCard widgets (now read from slice providers, not FutureProviders)
- `mobile/lib/features/journey/journey_controller.dart` — xpGainedThisWalk, levelUpTo, achievementUnlocked state
- `mobile/lib/features/journey/journey_screen.dart` — XP counter in stats bar, level-up/achievement snackbars
- `mobile/lib/features/journey/celebration_dialog.dart` — XP earned display in celebration

### Schema
- `DailyMissions` table: unique index on (UserId, Date) for mission generation idempotency
- `UserAchievements` table: unique index on (UserId, AchievementId) for concurrent unlock safety
- `Users` table: TotalXp (bigint), Level (int), TotalHexesStolen (int), AllMissionsCompleteDays (int)

## Open Questions

- Should achievements be visible to other players? (Currently: yes, endpoint is [Authorize] but no IDOR check — by design, like profile badges)
- Achievement-triggered level-up not surfaced as separate level-up banner to client (only achievement toast shown) — minor UX gap
- Distance achievements use int truncation: 0.99km → 0% progress on "Walk 1km" — acceptable?

## Real-Time Push Integration (Delta Architecture)

**Mission progress pushed via `MissionDelta` event (SignalR, per-user group):**
- Fired after `RecordProgress` in `ProcessStepClaim`
- Payload: `{ updates: [{missionId, type, progress, target, completed, xpAwarded}], allMissionsBonus }`
- Flutter `missions_slice` applies delta without API call
- UI updates per-step during walk (not just after walk ends)

**Achievement unlocks pushed via `AchievementUnlocked` event:**
- Fired after `CheckAndUnlock` completes with new unlocks
- Payload: `{ unlocks: [{id, name, icon, category, xpAwarded}] }`
- Flutter `achievements_slice` appends unlock + triggers celebration UI
- No more "silent" achievement discovery only on home tab refresh

**XP pushed via `XpDelta` event:**
- Fired after `AwardXp` succeeds
- Payload: `{ xpGained, totalXp, level, leveledUp, progressXp, neededXp, progressPercent }`
- Flutter `xp_slice` applies — home page XP bar updates in real-time

**All fired AFTER `SaveChangesAsync` succeeds** — never on uncommitted state.
- Future: time-limited/seasonal achievements? Would require adding expiry fields to definitions.

sectionContent.Components:

sectionContent.Description: After a network partition resolved at Hospital B, 30 devices reconnected simultaneously and dumped 10+ minutes of buffered data. The rules engine processed these as real-time observations, triggering 500+ alerts in rapid succession. Nurses overwhelmed, alert system lost credibility.

- 09:22 — Network restored, 30 devices reconnect
- 09:22-09:25 — Ingestion receives burst of 10min buffered data from all devices
- 09:23 — Rules engine fires 500+ alerts (interpreting buffered data as live breaches)
- 09:25 — On-call engineer manually disables alerting for Hospital B

sectionContent.Description: Stripe occasionally delivers duplicate webhooks within milliseconds. Our processor was checking idempotency key AFTER starting the capture flow — race condition window allowed two captures to execute.
sectionContent.Root Cause: The idempotency check used a SELECT then INSERT pattern instead of atomic upsert. Two concurrent webhook deliveries could both pass the SELECT before either INSERT completed.

sectionContent.Impact: 3 merchants had double-captured payments (~$2,400 total). Refunds issued manually.

# Current Architecture

### Components
- **Deploy Controller**: Watches DeploymentRequest CRDs, translates to ArgoCD Application manifests
- **Canary Analyzer**: Runs Prometheus queries during canary rollout, auto-promotes or rolls back
- **Rollback Engine**: Reverts ArgoCD Application to previous Git SHA on failure detection
- **Deploy Dashboard**: SSE-powered real-time view of all active rollouts across clusters

### Known Behaviors
- Deploy flow: PR merged → Git tag → ArgoCD syncs → canary 10% → analyze 5min → promote to 100%
- Rollback trigger: error rate >1% or p99 latency >2x baseline during canary window
- Blue-green: only for stateful services (databases, queues) — switches DNS, not pods
- Deploy lock: only one deployment per service at a time (queues concurrent requests)

### Edge Cases
- Deploy during incident: deploy lock can be force-overridden by on-call engineer
- Canary with zero traffic: services with <10 RPS skip canary, go straight to rolling update
- Multi-cluster: canary runs in primary cluster first, then promotes to secondary clusters sequentially

## File Map
- `controllers/deploy_controller.go` — translates DeploymentRequest to ArgoCD manifests
- `controllers/canary/analyzer.go` — Prometheus-based canary health analysis
- `controllers/rollback/engine.go` — automated rollback on failure
- `apps/portal/pages/deployments.tsx` — real-time deploy dashboard

sectionContent.Description: Viewers of Stream A briefly saw segments from Stream B. Duration: ~45 seconds. Affected ~200 viewers.
sectionContent.Timeline:
- 14:32 — Seller reports "my viewers are seeing someone else's stream"
- 14:35 — Confirmed via CloudFront access logs: cache key collision between two streams
- 14:38 — Invalidated CloudFront cache for affected paths
- 14:40 — All viewers back on correct streams
sectionContent.Root Cause: CloudFront cache key only included path (`/streams/{id}/segment.ts`) but not the query string containing the signed token. Two streams with sequential IDs had overlapping segment numbers, and a cache edge served the wrong cached segment.
sectionContent.Fix: Added `stream_id` and `token_hash` to CloudFront cache key policy. Each stream now has a completely unique cache namespace regardless of path similarity.
sectionContent.Prevention:
- Cache key policy now includes Origin header + custom `X-Stream-ID` header
- Added integration test: two concurrent streams must never cross-contaminate at cache level

content.summary: Viewers of Stream A briefly saw segments from Stream B. Duration: ~45 seconds. Affected ~200 viewers.
content.markdown:
# Description
Viewers of Stream A briefly saw segments from Stream B. Duration: ~45 seconds. Affected ~200 viewers.

# Timeline
- 14:32 — Seller reports "my viewers are seeing someone else's stream"
- 14:35 — Confirmed via CloudFront access logs: cache key collision between two streams
- 14:38 — Invalidated CloudFront cache for affected paths
- 14:40 — All viewers back on correct streams

# Root Cause
CloudFront cache key only included path (`/streams/{id}/segment.ts`) but not the query string containing the signed token. Two streams with sequential IDs had overlapping segment numbers, and a cache edge served the wrong cached segment.

# Fix
Added `stream_id` and `token_hash` to CloudFront cache key policy. Each stream now has a completely unique cache namespace regardless of path similarity.

# Prevention
- Cache key policy now includes Origin header + custom `X-Stream-ID` header
- Added integration test: two concurrent streams must never cross-contaminate at cache level
